customManagers.description: Dockerfile ARG version pins (github-releases / github-tags / pypi) with a `# renovate:` marker on the line above -- the Dockerfile is the single source of truth for every component version (ci/read_pins.py)
Docker base images in ARGs: `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image> ...` above `ARG X=<image>:<tag>[@digest]`
libr4d: a raw commit SHA on Codeberg main, tracked as a git-refs digest (R4D_REPO must stay in sync with depName)

packageRules.description: setup-python pins the image's interpreter (the venv is Ubuntu 24.04's python 3.12; ci/check_constraints.py evaluates markers for it) -- it moves with the release base, not on its own

THE TWO IMAGE TRIGGERS, one group `stack` (branch renovate/stack-update, label `stack`): a vLLM release (github-releases) and a ROCm base image tag (docker, major/minor/patch). postUpgradeTasks run ci/resolve_stack.py --apply, which derives torch / triton / torchvision / aiter / transformers from them, regenerates constraints.txt, bumps VERSION and adds the CHANGELOG skeleton; exit non-zero (no matching AMD wheel, unparseable vLLM pins, unsupported ROCm major) leaves the PR red = incompatible, never merged. rebaseWhen=conflicted: Renovate rebases only on a conflict, so it does not fight the pushes of the Hermes re-anchor agent on this branch (and Renovate stops touching a branch with foreign commits anyway). The accept-night workflow merges it when every gate is green.
prBodyNotes: Automated stack update. `ci/resolve_stack.py --apply` derived every other pin from this vLLM release and ROCm base (see the commit and docs/MAINTENANCE.md). If the `resolve` check is red the stack is incompatible: no AMD wheel for it, or vLLM's pins could not be read. If `patch-dryrun` is red the Hermes re-anchor agent is called and pushes fixes to this branch. The nightly gate (accept-night, 04:00-06:00 Europe/Berlin) merges and releases this PR when every check and the GPU gate are green; nothing else does.

packageRules.description: ROCm base image: only a new TAG is an image change; a digest refresh of the same tag is not (docs/MAINTENANCE.md)

DISABLED -- torch / triton / torchvision. Derived, never bumped on its own (docs/MAINTENANCE.md): a new image version exists only for a vLLM release or a ROCm base tag, and ci/resolve_stack.py derives this pin from them. (resolve_stack: vLLM's docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base names release/X.Y, the triton commit and the torchvision tag; AMD's whl-next index must carry them for the base image's ROCm.)

DISABLED -- aiter. Derived, never bumped on its own (docs/MAINTENANCE.md): a new image version exists only for a vLLM release or a ROCm base tag, and ci/resolve_stack.py derives this pin from them. (resolve_stack: vLLM's AITER_BRANCH; a deliberate hold is an entry in ci/stack_overrides.json.)

DISABLED -- transformers. Derived, never bumped on its own (docs/MAINTENANCE.md): a new image version exists only for a vLLM release or a ROCm base tag, and ci/resolve_stack.py derives this pin from them. (resolve_stack: newest PyPI release inside the range of vLLM's requirements/common.txt.)

DISABLED -- libr4d (git-refs digest), rocm_bandwidth_test and the ubuntu release-base digest. Owner decision 2026-10-07: no feature development, the image changes only for a vLLM release or a ROCm base tag; libr4d moves with a GPU A/B by a human, the other two are not worth an image version.

DISABLED -- image Python dependencies (constraints.txt). Regenerated by ci/resolve_stack.py --apply (check_constraints.py --update) on a stack PR; ci/check_constraints.py proves it on every PR. The GENERATED rules below stay: that script maintains and checks them.
